input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more details.
Yes, the MMS issue is happening on the number I provided—555-123-2002. That’s the only line I’m using right now.
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see the Airplane Mode icon is on, and my battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons at the moment. What should I do next?
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, I see a “No Signal” icon and it says “Data Disabled.” There are still no signal bars showing. What should I try next?
It looks like my phone is saying “No SIM card detected.” What should I do to fix this?

I just tried, but my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. There’s no specific error message—it just won’t go through. What should I check next?
I checked my APN settings, and it looks like the MMSC URL isn’t set at all. Could this be why MMS isn’t working? What should I do to fix it?
I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone, but unfortunately, I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else I should try? It’s getting a bit frustrating that it’s still not working.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending an MMS again?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending an MMS again, but it still won’t go through. Is there anything else I should check or try?

I checked my messaging app’s permissions—it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see storage permission listed. Should I enable storage permission for the messaging app and try sending an MMS again?
I’ve enabled storage permission for the messaging app and tried sending an MMS again, but it still isn’t working. Is there anything else I can try to get this fixed?

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, your full name and date of birth, or your customer ID? This will help me check your line and service status.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more details.

Thank you for providing your details, John. I have identified your account. To help resolve your MMS issue, I’ll need to check a few things about your line and service.

Could you please confirm which phone number (or line) you are experiencing the MMS issue with, especially if you have multiple lines on your account? Is it the number you provided (555-123-2002), or a different one?
Yes, the MMS issue is happening on the number I provided—555-123-2002. That’s the only line I’m using right now.

Thank you for confirming. To troubleshoot your MMS issue, I’ll guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. 

First, could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (and how many)
- If you see any icons like “Airplane Mode,” “4G,” “5G,” or “E”
- If mobile data is enabled

This will help determine if there are any basic connectivity issues affecting MMS.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see the Airplane Mode icon is on, and my battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons at the moment. What should I do next?

Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including cellular service and mobile data, which are required for sending MMS messages. 

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once it’s off, wait a few seconds and check if your signal bars and mobile data icons reappear. Let me know what you see after turning off Airplane Mode.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, I see a “No Signal” icon and it says “Data Disabled.” There are still no signal bars showing. What should I try next?

Thank you for the update. Since you’re seeing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” let’s check if your SIM card is being recognized by your phone. 

Please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings and let me know if it shows as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the steps.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It looks like my phone is saying “No SIM card detected.” What should I do to fix this?

Your phone is not detecting the SIM card, which explains why you have no signal or data. The next step is to reseat your SIM card. Please power off your phone, remove the SIM card, carefully reinsert it, and then power your phone back on. 

After you’ve done this, let me know if your phone now detects the SIM card and if you see any signal bars or data icons.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve reinserted the SIM card and turned my phone back on. Now I see one bar of signal (it says “Poor”) and “2G” is showing, but data is still disabled. What should I do next?

Now that your SIM card is detected and you have some signal, let’s work on improving your connection and enabling mobile data, as MMS requires at least a 3G connection and mobile data to function.

Please try the following steps:
1. Enable mobile data on your phone.
2. If possible, change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G (look for an option like “4G/5G preferred” in your network settings).

After making these changes, let me know:
- If mobile data is now enabled
- If your signal improves to 3G, 4G, or 5G

If you need help with these steps, let me know your phone model and I can provide more detailed instructions.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned on mobile data and set the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now my status bar shows excellent signal strength, “5G,” and data is enabled. What should I do next to try sending MMS?

Great! Your phone now has excellent signal strength, 5G connectivity, and mobile data enabled—these are all required for MMS to work.

Please try sending an MMS message now. If it still doesn’t work, let me know what error or issue you see, and we can continue troubleshooting (such as checking APN settings or app permissions).
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried, but my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. There’s no specific error message—it just won’t go through. What should I check next?

Since you have good signal and mobile data, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Please check your APN settings and look for the MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL. Let me know if the MMSC URL is set or if it’s missing/incorrect. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through the process.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings, and it looks like the MMSC URL isn’t set at all. Could this be why MMS isn’t working? What should I do to fix it?

Yes, a missing MMSC URL in your APN settings will prevent MMS from working. To fix this, please reset your APN settings to the default values in your phone’s network settings.

After resetting the APN settings, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Once your phone restarts, try sending an MMS again and let me know if it works.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone, but unfortunately, I still can’t send MMS messages. Is there anything else I should try? It’s getting a bit frustrating that it’s still not working.

Thank you for your patience. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, rebooted your phone, and still can’t send MMS, let’s check a few more things:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your device? Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. If it’s on, please turn it off and try sending an MMS again.
2. Does your messaging app have the necessary permissions (storage and SMS)? If not, please grant these permissions.

Please check these two items and let me know if making these changes allows you to send MMS. If you need help with either step, let me know your phone model and I can provide detailed instructions.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending an MMS again?

Yes, please turn off Wi-Fi Calling on your device and then try sending an MMS message again. Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling enabled can interfere with MMS delivery.

Let me know if turning off Wi-Fi Calling resolves the issue or if you still experience problems sending MMS.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending an MMS again, but it still won’t go through. Is there anything else I should check or try?

Let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS. Please verify that your messaging app has both “storage” and “SMS” permissions enabled in your phone’s app settings.

If either permission is missing, please enable it and then try sending an MMS again. Let me know if you need help finding these settings or if granting permissions resolves the issue.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.

I checked my messaging app’s permissions—it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see storage permission listed. Should I enable storage permission for the messaging app and try sending an MMS again?

Yes, please enable storage permission for your messaging app. MMS messages often require access to storage to send or receive media files.

After granting storage permission, try sending an MMS again and let me know if it works. If you still have issues, please let me know what happens when you try to send the message.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I’ve enabled storage permission for the messaging app and tried sending an MMS again, but it still isn’t working. Is there anything else I can try to get this fixed?

You’ve already tried all the standard troubleshooting steps: checking signal, enabling mobile data, resetting APN settings, rebooting, disabling Wi-Fi Calling, and granting necessary app permissions. Since MMS is still not working after these steps, your issue may require advanced technical support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can assist you further with this problem. Please hold on while I connect you.
